cards.text: Midian is beaten, and the Israelites come to Gideon with a BIG offer: “Rule over us—you and your son and grandson—for you have saved us from the hand of Midian.” Three generations! The best offer I ever got was the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: The Israelites want Gideon, his son and his grandson to rule over them. What's Gideon's answer?

answers.text: The LORD will rule over you
My son will rule in my place
I will rule until Midian is gone

cards.text: So Gideon won't rule over them, and neither will his son, but he does ask each man for an earring from his plunder. The enemies were Ishmaelites, so those earrings are gold.

cards.question: When Gideon asks each man for an earring, the Israelites grumble and hold on to their plunder.

cards.text: Earring after earring lands on a spread-out garment: 1,700 shekels of gold, plus crescent ornaments, pendants, the purple garments of Midian's kings and the chains off the camels' necks. Even the CAMELS had to hand over their jewelry!

cards.question: Gideon now has all that gold and royal goods. What does he make from it all?
Gideon places his ephod in Ophrah, his hometown. What does all Israel soon start doing there?
Once all Israel worships Gideon's ephod, it turns out to be a blessing for Gideon and his household.

cards.text: Meanwhile, Midian is down, and it STAYS down. It never raises its head again.

cards.question: With Midian subdued and never raising its head again, what does the land have in the days of Gideon?

cards.text: Then Jerubbaal son of Joash, that's Gideon, goes home and settles down. After all those battles, I bet he was ready for a NAP.

cards.question: Gideon had seventy sons of his own. Why so many?

cards.text: SEVENTY sons, and I thought six little cookie cutters made my counter CROWDED! And there's one more son, born to Gideon's concubine.
She lives in Shechem, and Gideon names the boy Abimelech. Later, Gideon dies at a ripe old age and is buried in the tomb of his father Joash in Ophrah.

cards.question: As soon as Gideon is dead, what do the Israelites do?

answers.text: Ask Gideon's sons to lead them

cards.question: After Gideon dies, the Israelites remember the LORD their God who delivered them from all their enemies on every side.
Gideon did a lot of good for Israel. How do the Israelites treat the house of Jerubbaal after he's gone?

answers.text: They give it land in Ophrah
They make it rich with gold

cards.text: And that's where we'll pause, friend. Keep that apron tied, because this story is FAR from finished.

findings.problem: The joke 'The best offer I ever got was the back of a junk drawer' doesn't pass the joke logic test. The core action in the fact is being offered something. Papa Dorin was never offered the drawer; he was slid into it. The line also contradicts his backstory, where his best offer was the angel's invitation from the Most High to bake for the Marriage Supper.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The joke changes Papa Dorin's own story by ranking the junk drawer as his best offer, which overwrites the angel's invitation in his backstory.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: 'Meanwhile' adds a time link that isn't in the text. Judges 8:28 says 'In this way Midian was subdued,' which ties the result to the victory, not to the same moment as the ephod.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The joke 'I bet he was ready for a NAP' reads like a nice dad being pleasant, not a laugh-out-loud line.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The question says the seventy sons were 'of his own.' That rules out both wrong answers (adopted boys from Midian, raising his brothers' sons), so the right answer is given away.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'Turn to worshiping other gods' doesn't use the text's own names: 'the Baals' and 'Baal-berith as their god' (Judges 8:33). Baal-berith never appears anywhere in the walkthrough, so the baker misses a key detail of the passage.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Because Baal-berith is never named, the baker leaves without an important detail of Judges 8:33.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The stop has 7 multiple choice cards, 3 true or false cards and 0 fill in the blank cards. Multiple choice dominates by a wide margin.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Card 18 is only the 'story isn't over' line and retells nothing from Judges 8:35, yet it cites Judges 8:35. The rule says a story card cites exactly the verses it tells, but a card that tells no verses still needs a 'verses' value.
findings.question: What should the 'verses' field be on a final story card that is only the 'story isn't over' line and tells no verses?
